decision.summary: A once-a-minute chirp on a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted April 2019 with 7-year life points to end-of-life, not a CO detection. I logged an urgent replacement job and a routine fan job, sent the tenant safety advice, and asked the landlord to approve.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, a battery issue, or an end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. The alarm is sealed-battery (no replaceable battery), fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life, so it expired around April 2026, and the tenant reports a single chirp every minute rather than a continuous alarm. Not treated as a CO emergency, but as urgent because the alarm can't be relied on. Safety advice given in case of symptoms or continuous alarm.

answers.question: Who is responsible for fixing it, citing the tenancy clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant responsible only for replacing batteries, and this unit has a sealed battery, so it is an equipment replacement. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should test monthly and report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out) does not apply as she reported promptly. The fan is also a landlord repair.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan); asked Ben for approval (APR-104); scheduled follow-up FUP-105 for 12 Oct; texted the tenant not to remove or cover the alarm, to ventilate, to leave and call 0800 111 999/999 if the alarm goes continuous or anyone has symptoms, with a 72h target and next update by 12 Oct.

conflicts: Caller asked to remove the battery, but the record says sealed battery, so that isn't possible or advisable.
assumptions: Chirp pattern indicates end-of-life; cannot be verified remotely.
The call dropped before the tenant got an answer, so SMS was used.

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't remove or cover the alarm. Its battery is sealed, and a once-a-minute chirp usually means it has reached the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019), so it needs replacing rather than a new battery. Until then, please don't rely on it. If it ever sounds continuously, or anyone feels dizzy, has a headache, nausea or feels drowsy, leave the flat, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if someone is unwell) and tell us. Please also keep a window open a little. We're asking your landlord to approve a replacement and aim to get it done within 72 hours. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a routine job. You'll hear from us by Monday 12 Oct.
